paragraphs: (1) In the Mishnah: Berakhot 7:3; Sheviit 4:6; Bikkurim 1:10; Eruvin 1:7; Pesachim 7:1; Ketubbot 3:3; Sotah 8:5; Gittin 2:3; Bava Kamma 8:6; Bava Metzia 2:10; Sanhedrin 10:6; Makkot 2:7; Avodah Zarah 3:5; Horayot 2:5; Zevachim 8:12, 13:1, 2; Menachot 5:8; Chullin 4:3, 5:3, 8:4; Bekhorot 2:6, 8:1; Parah 1:2, 3:4; Niddah 5:8.
(2) His sons: Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Chanina, and Rabbi Yishmael. He erred, for Rabbi Yishmael was the son of Rabbi Yose ben Chalafta; see his entry.

(3) He was one of the four who entered when Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus died; see his entry. Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 45a, write: this appears to imply that Rabbi Yose HaGelili was older than Rabbi Akiva, and so forth. Gittin 83a likewise mentions Rabbi Yose HaGelili before Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah and Rabbi Akiva. This is puzzling, for at the end of Eizehu Mekoman, 57a, ‘a student named Rabbi Yose HaGelili, who first came to the study house,’ told Rabbi Tarfon, ‘Master,’ and so forth. In Eruvin 53b, Beruryah, Rabbi Meir’s wife—he was among Rabbi Akiva’s later students—told him, ‘Foolish Galilean!’ He should have said briefly, ‘Which way to Lod?’ It appears that Rabbi Yose HaGelili was Rabbi Akiva’s student-colleague and younger than he, although Gittin mentions him before Rabbi Akiva, just as the Passover Haggadah mentions Rabbi Akiva before Rabbi Tarfon, although Rabbi Tarfon was his teacher, as implied by Ketubbot, chapter 9; see the beginning of Shenei Dayyanei Gezerot. At the end of Moed Katan, when Rabbi Yishmael’s sons died, four elders came to console him: Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yose HaGelili, Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, and Rabbi Akiva. In Ellu Naarot, the Rosh writes that he was Rabbi Akiva’s colleague. In Ein Doreshin 14a he said: ‘Akiva, how long will you make the Divine Presence profane?’ In Avot de-Rabbi Natan, chapter 1, he spoke in Rabbi Akiva’s name. Sifrei, Chukkat, and Yalkut there reveal his wisdom: at Yavneh they permitted the flesh of a cow that drank purification water. This was one of the matters Rabbi Yose HaGelili argued before Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Akiva dismissed him; afterwards he found an answer. He asked him: ‘May I return?’ He replied: ‘Not everyone, but you, for you are Yose HaGelili,’ and so forth. Rabbi Tarfon said: ‘I saw the ram goring west, north, and south, doing as it wished and growing great’—this is Rabbi Akiva—‘and behold, the male goat came’—this is Rabbi Yose HaGelili—‘and cast him to the ground and trampled him, and none rescued him from his hand.’ A similar incident appears at the end of Eizehu Mekoman, cited above. Sifrei, Korach: when Rabbi Yose HaGelili first came to serve before the sages, he said: ‘Master, the sin offering—he shall give it to the priest,’ and so forth. Rabbi Tarfon was silent. Rabbi Akiva sprang up and told him: ‘My son, thus I expound,’ and so forth. Everywhere: Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Yose HaGelili, and Rabbi Akiva. In Sotah, chapter 8: ‘Rabbi Yose HaGelili says: He returns from the battle lines,’ and so forth; ‘Rabbi Yose says,’ and so forth. In the Tosefta Rabbi Yose spoke in Rabbi Yose HaGelili’s name. This proves that the unqualified Rabbi Yose is not Rabbi Yose HaGelili; rather, the unqualified Rabbi Yose is ben Chalafta. Dorot Olam wrote that Rabbi Yose HaKohen was Rabbi Yose HaGelili. This too is incorrect: Rabbi Yose HaKohen was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s student, whereas Rabbi Tarfon was Rabbi Yose HaGelili’s teacher. How could Rabbi Yose HaKohen argue before Rabbi Akiva, who was a student of Rabbi Eliezer, who was a student of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai?

(4) Bereshit Rabbah, section 17; Jerusalem Talmud, Almanah Nizonet, halakhah 3; and Vayikra Rabbah, Behar: Rabbi Yose HaGelili married his sister’s daughter, and she treated him contemptuously, and so forth. Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah gave his wife her ketubbah, and he divorced her. She married another, became poor, and Rabbi Yose HaGelili supported her, as it says, ‘Do not hide yourself from your own flesh.’ It appears there that he was Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah’s teacher. Avot de-Rabbi Natan, end of chapter 18: ‘He gathers carefully, without arrogance.’ His son died, and he gave another permission to speak on his behalf: Semachot, chapter 10. See above, Rabbi Yose ben Chalafta.

(5) Above Kefar Delata, at the mountaintop, is his burial. His son Rabbi Elazar was buried in the village. Outside the village, beneath the Mount of Olives, Rabbi Hillel was buried; this is not Hillel the Elder (גא״י; provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael). Benjamin’s Travels places Rabbi Yose HaGelili’s burial at Kedesh Naphtali. See Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh.

(6) Rabbi Eliezer speaks in his name: Zevachim 44b. Rabbi Elazar ben Teradyon lived in his generation. Rabbi Chanina ben Chakhinai was frequently before him. Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel disputes with him in the Mishnah, Menachot 63a: ‘Rabbi Yose HaGelili’s words; Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says.’ And Rabbi Chananyah, son of Rabbi Yehoshua’s brother. The unqualified Rabbi Yehudah is bar Ilai, his student. Rabbi was his student, Tosafot, Menachot 38b; this requires examination, for it seems remote to me; see his entry. In Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri’s name: Kiddushin 39a. Rabbi Yochanan in Rabbi Yose HaGelili’s name: Temurah 3a and Vayikra Rabbah, section 34. Rabbi Yose ben Dormaskit transmitted in his name, as did Abba Yose ben Dostai, Rabbi Natan HaBavli, and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar: Chullin 75b (75a:2 in the linked edition).
